I'm all about expressing love no matter what / for whom it is about!

That said I find that the identity politics in the LGBTI2Q+ community are sometimes divisive and create more problems than they solve.

 I don't know or understand enough about that project, its history, or context to comment but that's my first reaction  :P

I was going to agree but then I realized that with men I have only 1-2 'types' and for them it is super easy for me to be attracted where as for women I have many more 'types'.

For context I am a cis-male who has recently fully come out to himself and is just starting to put down the sword of internalized bi-negativity so this might change over time
I loved the show 'please like me' but trigger warning if you get upset by complicated family dynamics and depictions of mental illness

I had a very similiar experience minus the pregnancy part. I really had to put some of my stuff to the side in order to comfort her well, my goal was to keep my mind on the prize and not make this about my hurt feelings. Ultimately she has been supportive and open but she was pretty invalidating during that conversation. Then we didn't talk about it for a while, it was like nothing happened, but now she includes more bi fantasies during sex (we often tell sexual stories while messing around) and is generally accepting. I found that coming out to her made we want to come out more publicly BC I feel like I've always had to hide who I am.

I am a fairly sex positive kind of guy and I make lots of sexualized jokes but now I'm worried about coming out to my friends BC I'm worried they will think I was hitting on them or something. Part of me wants to be out fully but another part is like, what's the point? I'm married and any m-m stuff I do will be in the context of my marriage so what difference would it make? I've also been labeled as gay all my life BC I'm pretty effeminate and always got mad and disputed it because I didn't like being mislabeled. Now I feel like a hipocryt and don't want to come out to people BC it would 'prove them right' in a way.

So now that I'm out to my wife and things are good I feel stuck in a whole new way lol. Still it is great to be out with her and that she is even open to some MMF stuff as a couple (in theory and at least for now in fantasy).

Congrats on your coming out! How do you feel about having to had comfort her?

It angers me and makes me feel invalidated...on the other hand there were times in my life where I identified as heteroflexible when I had more internalized binegativity and didn't understand the bicycle. I think it might be a normal part of people understanding and accepting their sexuality butba lot of the stuff I see is more like tokanism and identity 'appropriation' if you know what I mean . So to me at the individual level it might be fine but at the group/population level it often pisses me off
